title: Cyber insurance claims - what policies actually cover
p1: Think cyber insurance pays for anything that happens after a data breach? That assumption can turn a bad incident into an expensive surprise.
p2: Cyber policies can cover very different losses depending on the wording. Some may pay for breach investigation, legal costs, customer notification, data recovery, business interruption, ransomware response, or certain liability claims. But having a policy does not automatically mean every cyber-related loss is covered.
p3:
One detail many people miss: the cause of the incident can matter as much as the damage. A policy might respond to a network attack but have exclusions, conditions, or limits for social engineering fraud, unapproved payments, outdated security practices, or certain types of regulatory penalties. Coverage may also depend on whether the business followed the security controls it promised when buying the policy.

The practical takeaway? Don't judge cyber insurance by its headline coverage limit. Check what triggers coverage, what is excluded, the sub-limits, deductibles, and the obligations you must meet after an incident.
conclusion: If your business had a cyber incident tomorrow, would you know exactly which losses your policy would actually reimburse?
